effect_estimate.comment: Primary qualitative case study reporting thematic findings alongside descriptive interview proportions and municipal administrative figures rather than statistical causal effect estimates.
effect_estimate.value: Qualitative — no numeric effect estimate reported. Across interviews (n=20) and focus groups (n=14) in Amathole District Municipality, inequitable and unreliable rural water access was driven by non-implementation of municipal water by-laws and the Rural Household Connection Policy (stalled >1 year due to lack of political will, political interference, and financial constraints), non-registration of indigent households for Free Basic Water (resulting in unaffordable bills and a 27% municipal revenue collection rate vs. the 95% national standard, with 80% of the Equitable Share grant consumed by salaries and O&M at 2% vs. the 8% national standard), bloated administrative staffing with field skills shortages (reported by 50% and 30% of interviewed officials, respectively), unaddressed illegal connections, theft/vandalism, and dilapidated infrastructure.
effect_estimate.where_found: PDF p. 1, Abstract; PDF pp. 3-6, Sections 5.1-5.4 & Conclusions

mechanism_certainty.comment: Appraised with CASP Qualitative Checklist (design ceiling = 2). Assigned 2 because semi-structured interviews with municipal officials, councillors, Water Board representatives, and community focus groups plus municipal documents directly observe and document specific administrative/legal mechanisms impeding rural water access (stalled implementation of the Rural Household Connection Policy and municipal by-laws, indigent status non-registration causing unaffordable billing under the Free Basic Water framework, conditional grant underutilization, and non-enforcement against illegal connections).

mechanism_flags.comment: Examines rural vs. urban service jurisdiction and dispersed rural standpipes (ELIGIBILITY, service_area), stalled regularization via the Rural Household Connection Policy and indigent registration exemptions under Free Basic Water/Equitable Share (DISCRETION_ACCOMMODATION, hardship_exception, procedural_steps), billing/tariff non-affordability and >1-year policy / >2-week repair / grant-condition delays (BURDEN, fees, delay), weak by-law enforcement against illegal connections/vandalism and lack of municipal consequence management (ENFORCEMENT, sanction), and political interference, lack of political will, and national-municipal intergovernmental coordination (political_coordination).
mechanism_flags.value: ELIGIBILITY, BURDEN, DISCRETION_ACCOMMODATION, ENFORCEMENT, service_area, fees, procedural_steps, delay, hardship_exception, sanction, political_coordination

outcome_flags.comment: Directly examines rural water access disparities (water_access), household connections vs. shared standpipes and illegal connections under the Rural Household Connection Policy (formal_connection), unreliable, unsafe, and insufficient water supply (service_reliability, service_quality, service_quantity), multi-week supply interruptions from unfixed taps, pipe bursts, and cable theft (service_continuity), and billing affordability under the Free Basic Water / indigent framework (affordability).
outcome_flags.value: water_access, formal_connection, service_reliability, service_quantity, service_quality, service_continuity, affordability
